#BV FOR AC
```{r}
AC_22 <- read_csv(here::here("data_sheets/compiled_sheets/AC_compiledsheet_full_2022.csv")) 

library(dplyr)

#organize the data
AC_22 <- AC_22 %>%
  mutate(
    sample_ID = str_c(Year, Recipient, Gen, str_pad(Transect, width = 3, pad = "0"), Plant_ID, sep = "-"), #create an id column for each individual
    sample_ID = str_replace(sample_ID, "^([^_]*)_", "\\1-"), #use "_" rather than "-"
    F_plant = ifelse(F_plant == TRUE, 1, 0), #make fitness plant binary (1/0) rather than true/false
    Transect = as.numeric(Transect)) #make sure location is a continuous variable

#clean the data
AC_22 <- AC_22 %>%
  mutate(
    surv_to_flower = ifelse(total_fruits > 0 & surv_to_flower == 0, 1, surv_to_flower), #If a plant produced any fruits, it must have survived to flowering, even if the original surv_to_flower entry was coded as 0, This corrects miscodings where survival to flowering was mistakenly marked as 0 despite having fruit production
  ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Transect)) # We are removing W1 and W2 from these analyses because they were part of a different experiment involving a watered treatment. 
## In the original dataset, we included some extra fitness plants (see `anyFit_P`) in other transects for comparison with W1 and W2. 
### For the purposes of these analyses, we will exclude them and focus only on the `F_plant` values that are recorded for every segment.

AC_22$F_plant[is.na(AC_22$F_plant)] <- 0 #we need to make F_plant 0 and not NA

#Now we want to make sure every segment is represented by one F_plant (because we will filter by F_plant soon)
AC_22 <- AC_22 %>%
  mutate(sample_prefix = substr(sample_ID, 1, 19)) %>% #create a sample prefix with the first 19 characters of sample ID
  group_by(sample_prefix) %>% #group by the prefix
  mutate(
    all_dead = all(surv_to_flower == 0), #flags groups where no plants survived and where there are currently no fitness plants
##if a group has no fitness plants, it randomly assigns one plant in the group to be the fitness plant
    no_f_plant = sum(F_plant) == 0, 
    F_plant = if_else(
      no_f_plant & row_number() == sample(n(), 1),
      1L,
      F_plant
    ) #this will pick different individuals within the group each time unless you set a seed. For the purposes of this analyses, it will not matter because their values will be zero either way.
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-sample_prefix, -all_dead, -no_f_plant) #ungroup and remove the rows that were created\


#Now we want to determine how many individuals within a segment survived to flower
AC_22 <- AC_22 %>%
  mutate(group = ceiling(row_number() / 8)) %>%  # Create a grouping variable for every 8 rows
  # Calculate the sum of 'surv_to_flower' within each group
  group_by(group) %>%
  mutate(total_surv_to_flower = sum(surv_to_flower, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% # Ungroup to avoid grouped data frame
  # Remove the temporary 'group' column
  dplyr::select(-group)

# Filter to fitness plants once
AC_22 <- AC_22 %>%
  filter(F_plant == 1)
```

```{r}
AC_22 <- AC_22_filtered %>%
  group_by(Recipient) %>%
  mutate(
    avg_mat_fitness = mean(est_fecundity, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_mat_corolla = mean(corolla_diam_mm_SEG, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_mat_SLA     = mean(SLA_SEG, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_mat_d13C    = mean(d13C_SEG, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(Donor) %>%
  mutate(
    avg_pat_fitness = mean(avg_mat_fitness, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_pat_corolla = mean(avg_mat_corolla, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_pat_SLA     = mean(avg_mat_SLA, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_pat_d13C    = mean(avg_mat_d13C, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    avg_fitness = mean(avg_pat_fitness, na.rm = TRUE),
    BV_fitness  = avg_pat_fitness / avg_fitness
  )
```



```{r}
# list of traits you want to process
traits <- c("fitness", "corolla_diam_mm_SEG", "d13C_SEG", "SLA_SEG")

library(dplyr)

traits <- c("fitness", "corolla_diam_mm_SEG", "d13C_SEG", "SLA_SEG")

# For each trait, prefer "avg_mat_<trait>" if present; else use "<trait>"
source_cols <- setNames(
  ifelse(paste0("avg_mat_", traits) %in% names(AC_22),
         paste0("avg_mat_", traits),
         traits),
  traits
)

for (tr in traits) {
  src     <- source_cols[[tr]]                 # actual source col name in AC_22
  pat_col <- paste0("avg_pat_", tr)            # donor-mean col to create
  bv_col  <- paste0("BV_", tr)                 # BV col to create

  AC_22 <- AC_22 %>%
    group_by(Donor) %>%
    mutate(!!pat_col := mean(.data[[src]], na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(!!bv_col  := .data[[pat_col]] / mean(.data[[pat_col]], na.rm = TRUE))
}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(rlang)
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)

make_panel_obs <- function(dat, x_col, y_col, beta_x, x_lab,
                           y_lab = "AC genetic value: estimated fitness",
                           r_override = NULL) {
  x_sym <- rlang::ensym(x_col)
  y_sym <- rlang::ensym(y_col)

  d <- dat %>%
    dplyr::select(x = !!x_sym, y = !!y_sym) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      x = as.numeric(scale(x, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
      y = as.numeric(scale(y, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE))
    )

  if (nrow(d) < 3) stop("Not enough non-missing points for ellipse/correlation.")

  # raw BV correlation (just for the ellipse/feel)
  r_pair <- suppressWarnings(cor(d$x, d$y))

  # what to display: use override (from G-matrix) if supplied
  r_to_show <- if (is.null(r_override)) r_pair else r_override

  # arrow showing selection gradient direction
  ax <- sign(beta_x) * 0.6 * sd(d$x)
  ay <- 0.6 * sd(d$y)

  ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1) +
    stat_ellipse(level = 0.68, linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_segment(
  x = 0, y = 0, 
  xend = ax, yend = ay,
  arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm")), 
  linewidth = 0.7
)+
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf,
             label = paste0("r[A] = ", sprintf("%.3f", r_to_show)),
             hjust = 1.1, vjust = -0.6, size = 4.2) +
    labs(x = paste0("AC genetic value: ", x_lab), y = y_lab) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12)
}

# Official rA for AC 2022 G1
rA_vals <- list(
  corolla_diam = 0.511,
  SLA          = 0.322,
  d13C         = 0.120
)

# Named numeric vector; note the backticks for the name with a space
sel_grad <- c(`corolla diameter` = 0.323,
              SLA                = 0.591,
              dC13               = 0.041)

p_cd <- make_panel_obs(
  AC_22,
  x_col  = BV_corolla_diam_mm_SEG,
  y_col  = BV_fitness,
  beta_x = sel_grad["corolla diameter"],
  x_lab  = "corolla diameter",
  r_override = rA_vals$corolla_diam
)

p_sla <- make_panel_obs(AC_22, BV_SLA_SEG,  BV_fitness,
                        beta_x = sel_grad["SLA"],  x_lab = "SLA",
                        r_override = rA_vals$SLA)

p_dc  <- make_panel_obs(AC_22, BV_d13C_SEG, BV_fitness,
                        beta_x = sel_grad["dC13"], x_lab = "d13C",
                        r_override = rA_vals$d13C)

p_sla
p_dc

ggsave(
  filename = "quercus/figures_rcode/AC_BV.jpg",
  plot = (p_cd | p_sla) | p_dc,
  device = "jpg",
  dpi = 1200,
  width = 12, height = 5
)
```

#BV FOR BB
```{r}
BB_22 <- read_csv(here::here("data_sheets/compiled_sheets/BB_compiledsheet_full_2022.csv")) 

library(dplyr)

#organize the data
BB_22 <- BB_22 %>%
  mutate(
    sample_ID = str_c(Year, Recipient, Gen, str_pad(Location, width = 3, pad = "0"), Plant_ID, sep = "-"), #create an id column for each individual
    sample_ID = str_replace(sample_ID, "^([^_]*)_", "\\1-"), #use "_" rather than "-"
    F_plant = ifelse(F_plant == TRUE, 1, 0), #make fitness plant binary (1/0) rather than true/false
    Location = as.numeric(Location)) #make sure location is a continuous variable

#clean the data
BB_22 <- BB_22 %>%
  mutate(
    surv_to_flower = ifelse(total_fruits > 0 & surv_to_flower == 0, 1, surv_to_flower), #If a plant produced any fruits, it must have survived to flowering
  ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Location)) # remove W1 and W2

BB_22$F_plant[is.na(BB_22$F_plant)] <- 0 #make F_plant 0 and not NA

#Now we want to make sure every segment is represented by one F_plant
BB_22 <- BB_22 %>%
  mutate(sample_prefix = substr(sample_ID, 1, 19)) %>%
  group_by(sample_prefix) %>%
  mutate(
    all_dead = all(surv_to_flower == 0),
    no_f_plant = sum(F_plant) == 0, 
    F_plant = if_else(
      no_f_plant & row_number() == sample(n(), 1),
      1L,
      F_plant
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-sample_prefix, -all_dead, -no_f_plant)

#Now we want to determine how many individuals within a segment survived to flower
BB_22 <- BB_22 %>%
  mutate(group = ceiling(row_number() / 8)) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  mutate(total_surv_to_flower = sum(surv_to_flower, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-group)

#Filter to just fitness plants
BB_22_filtered <- BB_22 %>%
  filter(F_plant == 1)
```

```{r}
BB_22 <- BB_22_filtered %>%

  ) %>%

    avg_fitness = mean(avg_pat_fitness, na.rm = TRUE),
```

```{r}
BO_22 <- read_csv(here::here("data_sheets/compiled_sheets/BO_compiledsheet_full_2022.csv")) 

library(dplyr)

#organize the data
BO_22 <- BO_22 %>%
  mutate(
    sample_ID = str_c(Year, Recipient, Gen, str_pad(Transect, width = 3, pad = "0"), Plant_ID, sep = "-"), #create an id column for each individual
    sample_ID = str_replace(sample_ID, "^([^_]*)_", "\\1-"), #use "_" rather than "-"
    F_plant = ifelse(F_plant == TRUE, 1, 0), #make fitness plant binary (1/0) rather than true/false
    Transect = as.numeric(Transect)) #make sure location is a continuous variable

#clean the data
BO_22 <- BO_22 %>%
  mutate(
    surv_to_flower = ifelse(total_fruits > 0 & surv_to_flower == 0, 1, surv_to_flower), #If a plant produced any fruits, it must have survived to flowering
  ) %>%

BO_22$F_plant[is.na(BO_22$F_plant)] <- 0 #make F_plant 0 and not NA

#Now we want to make sure every segment is represented by one F_plant
BO_22 <- BO_22 %>%
  mutate(sample_prefix = substr(sample_ID, 1, 19)) %>%
  group_by(sample_prefix) %>%
  mutate(
    all_dead = all(surv_to_flower == 0),
    no_f_plant = sum(F_plant) == 0, 
    F_plant = if_else(
      no_f_plant & row_number() == sample(n(), 1),

      F_plant
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-sample_prefix, -all_dead, -no_f_plant)

#Now we want to determine how many individuals within a segment survived to flower

  mutate(group = ceiling(row_number() / 8)) %>%
```

```{r}
    sample_ID = str_c(Year, Recipient, Gen, str_pad(Transect, width = 3, pad = "0"), Plant_ID, sep = "-"), #create an id column for each individual
    sample_ID = str_replace(sample_ID, "^([^_]*)_", "\\1-"), #use "_" rather than "-"
    F_plant = ifelse(F_plant == TRUE, 1, 0), #make fitness plant binary (1/0) rather than true/false
    Transect = as.numeric(Transect)) #make sure location is a continuous variable

#clean the data
HR_22 <- HR_22 %>%
  mutate(
    surv_to_flower = ifelse(total_fruits > 0 & surv_to_flower == 0, 1, surv_to_flower), #If a plant produced any fruits, it must have survived to flowering
  ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Transect)) # remove W1 and W2

HR_22$F_plant[is.na(HR_22$F_plant)] <- 0 #make F_plant 0 and not NA

#Now we want to make sure every segment is represented by one F_plant
HR_22 <- HR_22 %>%
  mutate(sample_prefix = substr(sample_ID, 1, 19)) %>%
  group_by(sample_prefix) %>%
  mutate(
    all_dead = all(surv_to_flower == 0),
    no_f_plant = sum(F_plant) == 0, 
    F_plant = if_else(
      no_f_plant & row_number() == sample(n(), 1),
      1L,
      F_plant
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-sample_prefix, -all_dead, -no_f_plant)

#Now we want to determine how many individuals within a segment survived to flower
HR_22 <- HR_22 %>%
  mutate(group = ceiling(row_number() / 8)) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  mutate(total_surv_to_flower = sum(surv_to_flower, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-group)

#Filter to just fitness plants
HR_22 <- HR_22 %>%
  filter(F_plant == 1)

 HR_22 <- HR_22 %>%
   group_by(Recipient) %>%
   mutate(avg_mat_fitness = mean(est_fecundity, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
   ungroup()
 
 HR_22 <- HR_22 %>%
   group_by(Donor) %>%
   mutate(avg_pat_fitness = mean(avg_mat_fitness, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
   ungroup()
 
 HR_22 <- HR_22 %>%
   mutate(avg_fitness = mean(avg_pat_fitness, na.rm = TRUE))
 
 HR_22 <- HR_22 %>%
   mutate(BV_fitness = avg_pat_fitness/avg_fitness)
 
 HR_22 <-  HR_22 %>%
  group_by(Recipient) %>%
  mutate(avg_mat_corolla_diam_mm_SEG = mean(corolla_diam_mm_SEG, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

 HR_22 <-  HR_22 %>%
  group_by(Donor) %>%
  mutate(avg_pat_corolla_diam_mm_SEG = mean(avg_mat_corolla_diam_mm_SEG, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

HR_22 <-  HR_22 %>%
   mutate(avg_corolla_diam = mean(avg_pat_corolla_diam_mm_SEG, na.rm = TRUE))
 
 HR_22 <-  HR_22 %>%
  group_by(Recipient) %>%
  mutate(avg_mat_SLA_SEG = mean(SLA_SEG, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

 HR_22 <-  HR_22 %>%
  group_by(Donor) %>%
  mutate(avg_pat_SLA_SEG = mean(avg_mat_SLA_SEG, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
 
 HR_22 %>%
   mutate(avg_SLA = mean(avg_pat_SLA_SEG, na.rm = TRUE))
 
 HR_22 <-  HR_22 %>%
  group_by(Recipient) %>%
  mutate(avg_mat_d13C_SEG = mean(d13C_SEG, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

HR_22 <-  HR_22 %>%
  group_by(Donor) %>%
  mutate(avg_pat_d13C_SEG = mean(avg_mat_d13C_SEG, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()
 
 HR_22 %>%
   mutate(avg_d13C = mean(avg_pat_d13C_SEG, na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r}
# list of traits you want to process
traits <- c("fitness", "corolla_diam_mm_SEG", "d13C_SEG", "SLA_SEG")

library(dplyr)

traits <- c("fitness", "corolla_diam_mm_SEG", "d13C_SEG", "SLA_SEG")

# For each trait, prefer "avg_mat_<trait>" if present; else use "<trait>"
source_cols <- setNames(
  ifelse(paste0("avg_mat_", traits) %in% names( HR_22),
         paste0("avg_mat_", traits),
         traits),
  traits
)

for (tr in traits) {
  src     <- source_cols[[tr]]                 # actual source col name in  BO_22
  pat_col <- paste0("avg_pat_", tr)            # donor-mean col to create
  bv_col  <- paste0("BV_", tr)                 # BV col to create

 HR_22 <-  HR_22 %>%
    group_by(Donor) %>%
    mutate(!!pat_col := mean(.data[[src]], na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(!!bv_col  := .data[[pat_col]] / mean(.data[[pat_col]], na.rm = TRUE))
}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(rlang)
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)

make_panel_obs <- function(dat, x_col, y_col, beta_x, x_lab,
                           y_lab = "HR genetic value: estimated fitness",
                           r_override = NULL) {
  x_sym <- rlang::ensym(x_col)
  y_sym <- rlang::ensym(y_col)

  d <- dat %>%
    dplyr::select(x = !!x_sym, y = !!y_sym) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      x = as.numeric(scale(x, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)),
      y = as.numeric(scale(y, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE))
    )

  if (nrow(d) < 3) stop("Not enough non-missing points for ellipse/correlation.")

  # raw BV correlation (just for the ellipse/feel)
  r_pair <- suppressWarnings(cor(d$x, d$y))

  # what to display: use override (from G-matrix) if supplied
  r_to_show <- if (is.null(r_override)) r_pair else r_override

  # arrow showing selection gradient direction
  ax <- sign(beta_x) * 0.6 * sd(d$x)
  ay <- 0.6 * sd(d$y)

  ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1) +
    stat_ellipse(level = 0.68, linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_segment(
  x = 0, y = 0, 
  xend = ax, yend = ay,
  arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm")), 
  linewidth = 0.7
)+
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf,
             label = paste0("r[A] = ", sprintf("%.3f", r_to_show)),
             hjust = 1.1, vjust = -0.6, size = 4.2) +
    labs(x = paste0("HR genetic value: ", x_lab), y = y_lab) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12)
}

# Official rA for HR 2022 G1
rA_vals <- list(
  corolla_diam = 1.027,
  SLA          = NA,
  d13C         = -1.235
)

# Named numeric vector; note the backticks for the name with a space
sel_grad <- c(`corolla diameter` = 0.290,
              SLA                = -0.158,
              dC13               = -0.184)

p_cd <- make_panel_obs(
  HR_22,
  x_col  = BV_corolla_diam_mm_SEG,
  y_col  = BV_fitness,
  beta_x = sel_grad["corolla diameter"],
  x_lab  = "corolla diameter",
  r_override = rA_vals$corolla_diam
)

p_sla <- make_panel_obs(HR_22, BV_SLA_SEG,  BV_fitness,
                        beta_x = sel_grad["SLA"],  x_lab = "SLA",
                        r_override = rA_vals$SLA)

p_dc  <- make_panel_obs(HR_22, BV_d13C_SEG, BV_fitness,
                        beta_x = sel_grad["dC13"], x_lab = "d13C",
                        r_override = rA_vals$d13C)

(fig <- (p_cd | p_sla) | p_dc)

ggsave(
  filename = "quercus/figures_rcode/HR_BV.jpg",
  plot = (p_cd | p_sla) | p_dc,
  device = "jpg",
  dpi = 1200,
  width = 12, height = 5
)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

#prep
df_plot <- read_csv("quercus/figures_rcode/quercus_results.csv") %>%
  transmute(
    Pop,
    # pull "2022 G1", "2023 G1", "2023 G2" from "AC 2022 G1" etc.
    Env   = sub("^[A-Z]+\\s+", "", Population),
    trait = recode(trait,
                   est_fit       = "fecundity",
                   corolla_diam  = "corolla diameter",
                   SLA           = "SLA",
                   dC13          = "dC13"),
    raw_means,
    raw_means_se
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # facet order and x-axis order to match your reference
    trait = factor(trait, levels = c("corolla diameter", "dC13", "fecundity", "SLA")),
    Env   = factor(Env,   levels = c("2022 G1", "2023 G1", "2023 G2")),
    Pop   = factor(Pop,   levels = c("AC","BB","BO","HR"))
  )

p <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = Env, y = raw_means, color = Pop, shape = Pop)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = raw_means - raw_means_se, 
                    ymax = raw_means + raw_means_se),
                width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.6) +   # <- SE bars
  facet_wrap(~ trait, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Year × Generation", y = "Trait mean",
       color = "Population", shape = "Population") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17, 15, 18)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    AC = "#F8766D",  # red
    BB = "#7CAE00",  # green
    BO = "#00BFC4",  # teal
    HR = "#C77CFF"   # purple
  ))

p

P <- p + theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

P

# save
ggsave('quercus/figures_rcode/trait_means.jpg', P, device = "jpg", 
       dpi = 1200, width = 8, height = 6)
```

AC Correlation 2022
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

#G-matrix for AC 2022 G1
G_AC22 <- matrix(c(
  143.53433,  8.148266, 14.926858,  1.043195,
    8.148266,  1.768103,  2.693436, -0.275527,
   14.926858,  2.693436,  2.271721,  0.137218,
    1.043195, -0.275527,  0.137218,  0.529539
), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE)

colnames(G_AC22) <- rownames(G_AC22) <- c("est_fit", "corolla", "SLA", "d13C")

# Convert to correlation matrix
G_cor <- cov2cor(G_AC22)

# Melt for ggplot
df <- melt(G_cor)

a <- ggplot(df, aes(Var1, Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2))) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Genetic correlation matrix: AC 2022 G1",
       fill = "rA")
```
